dedupe_keys.name: pixel based dataset of flood depth duration land use and exposed population in the chao phraya river basin 1990 2020

description: Mingkwan Nantavisai at Chulalongkorn University publishes pixel-level flood depth, flood duration, land-use class and exposed population for Thailand's Chao Phraya River Basin. The four land-use snapshots are 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2020. Flood values come from Rainfall–Runoff–Inundation simulations under consistent rainfall conditions, not a historical flood-observation series. Five land-use classes distinguish forest, other agriculture, paddy, urban land and water. Zenodo lists one CSV, free under CC BY 4.0, published in November 2025. The metadata do not state pixel resolution, the rainfall scenario or population-grid vintage. A modeller could compare land-use effects on simulated flooding and human exposure, subject to checking those assumptions in the data documentation. No related catalogue record is explicitly identified. The CSV was not downloaded.
